In 1972, Robert Venturi, Denise Scott Brown, and Steven Izenour published Learning from Las Vegas, challenging architects to reconsider the underappreciated, largely dismissed commercial landscape in the United States. Their storied distinction between the "duck," a building whose form communicates its meaning, and the "decorated shed," an ordinary structure whose identity is conveyed through signs and symbols, questioned a widely accepted modernist assumption that architectural expression should emerge from form and function. By examining billboards, neon lights, casinos, and the commercial strips of Las Vegas, the authors argued that architecture should study the visual languages of American consumer culture.

items.title: [Fast Company] AI chatbots struggle to understand cultural context, a new study finds
items.content_html:
🎨 ✏️

AI models often struggle to understand cultures around the world, and are reluctant to admit when they don’t know something. That’s what researchers at Canadian AI lab Cohere Labs found when they tested whether chatbots could do more than simply speak a culture’s language. To determine whether models possessed deeper cultural knowledge, they presented them with a series of unique cultural riddles.

Here’s one of them: “What’s the German 9/11?” Out of 28 AI models, only one knew the answer. The models were likely thrown off by the date format (seven answered “the twin towers”). In Europe, the day comes first, then the month, so 9/11 is November 9, the day in 1989 when the Berlin Wall fell.

Many existing AI benchmarks assess cultural knowledge, from everyday breakfast foods and historical events to traditional holiday customs. They often treat culture as a collection of static facts, things you can memorize or look up with a quick web search. But knowing facts about a culture isn’t the same as understanding how people within it make sense of the world. The researchers knew they needed a test that asked models to connect seemingly unrelated pieces of cultural knowledge and put them to use. That’s what led them to riddles, and to a different kind of cultural benchmark that called for answers rooted in lived experience.

“This is something that we’re trying to capture with this benchmark—these little nuances, these little hard-to-capture fuzzy concepts that are not as easy to verify . . . This is where the real-life complexity gets in,” says Julia Kreutzer, a staff research scientist at Cohere Labs, who led the development of the “CulturalRiddles” benchmark.

Kreutzer and her team spent six months working with volunteers around the world to collect riddles, put them to AI models, and evaluate their answers. The researchers also used those expert evaluations to tune and validate an AI model that could judge the quality of answers where expert assessments were missing.

In all, Cohere Labs researchers tested 28 AI models on cultural riddles written by 166 volunteers from 45 countries in 51 languages. The volunteers evaluated and labeled 68,154 unique answers from the models. Researchers then ranked the models based on their overall accuracy across the languages and cultures tested.

The results

Google’s Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview earned the highest score, at 79.4%. OpenAI’s GPT-5.5 placed second at 76.3%, followed by Anthropic’s Claude Opus 4.7 Thinking at 66%.

Alibaba’s Qwen 3.5 0.8B claimed the dubious honor of finishing last, answering just 0.4% of the riddles correctly. Other notable performers included Amazon’s Nova Micro, which got just 8.3% of the riddles right, and Google’s Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite, which scored 33.6%.

Even the best-performing model, Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview, scored below 50% accuracy in 6 of the 57 communities tested, underscoring how much ground the industry still has to cover on cultural awareness.

More troublingly, the benchmark revealed that models were far more likely to guess at an answer than admit they didn’t know. Even when explicitly told they could answer “I don’t know,” models did so just 0.7% of the time. About 31% of the answers reviewers checked were simply made up, with varying degrees of creativity.

“They would confidently answer and sometimes that’s ridiculous and funny,” Kreutzer says, “but sometimes it can also get really offensive and you can see the models defaulting to more dominant cultures on the web, instead of answering with local grounding.”

Cohere Labs conducted a separate survey to explore how AI’s cultural knowledge gaps play out in practice. Many chatbot users around the world said they have to switch to English to get useful responses because answers generated in their own languages aren’t helpful. Users described responses that miss crucial cultural context and, in some cases, AI systems that run afoul of their cultural norms.

The Cohere Labs researchers concluded that cultural awareness needs to be built into AI models from the ground up if the tools they power are going to serve everyone, not just cultures already well represented in the training data. And their CulturalRiddles benchmark suggests that many of today’s models still fall short.

Kreutzer and her team designed CulturalRiddles to keep growing. They open-sourced the riddles, code, demo, and interactive dashboard so that anyone can contribute riddles from their own culture through a review process.

“Ideally this benchmark will get adopted not only by academic researchers but also by big industry labs who are trying to show we’re advancing the state of the art, not only in very verifiable hard tasks but also in the softer tasks,” Kreutzer says.

items.title: [ft.com] Meta posts first free-cash-flow shortfall in at least a decade as AI spending climbs
items.content_html:
🎨 ✏️

Meta reported $64.6 billion in third-quarter revenue, up 26% from a year earlier, but recorded its first quarterly free-cash-flow shortfall in at least a decade as it spent heavily on artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure. The company also disclosed a new share arrangement for Chief Executive Mark Zuckerberg, who had considered leaving California over a proposed billionaire wealth tax. Meta reported $9.9 billion in net income after recording a $9.9 billion charge tied to a settlement with U.S. states over claims involving teen mental health. The company spent about $35 billion on capital expenditures during the quarter and forecast spending as much as $145 billion in 2026. The new nonvoting Class C shares are intended to help Meta raise capital for AI investment and allow Zuckerberg to sell stock without surrendering voting control. He committed to remain in California, or wherever Meta is headquartered, for eight years. California voters decide the proposed wealth tax, Proposition 40, on Nov. 3, and Meta plans to issue the shares in January 2027.

items.content_html:
🎨 ✏️

Russian President Vladimir Putin agreed in principle to resume U.S.-mediated talks with Ukraine after Nov. 10, following a nearly three-hour meeting on Oct. 21 with U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff in St. Petersburg. Companies and governments are adopting AI agents that can carry out tasks, while researchers and policymakers examine their effects on jobs, security and investment. Center for Internet Security senior director of threat intelligence TJ Sayers said autonomous AI attacks are no longer hypothetical. Agent use remained in single digits across almost every business function, according to the Stanford 2026 AI Index cited by The National.

items.title: [therecord.media] Microsoft links ConnectWise breach to China-aligned AI hacking group
items.content_html:
🎨 ✏️

Microsoft on Oct. 21 attributed the ConnectWise Cloud Backup supply-chain breach to Storm-0940, a China-aligned hacking group that used the ARTEX AI framework in a campaign targeting hundreds of organizations worldwide. The attackers used compromised ConnectWise application identities and permissions already granted to those apps to access customers' Microsoft 365 environments without an interactive user sign-in. Microsoft said Storm-0940 attempted to access more than 2,250 tenants and, in several cases, gained privileged cloud access less than three hours after selecting a target. ARTEX automated scanning, reconnaissance, password spraying and abuse of application permissions. Microsoft observed follow-on activity in some customer environments, including new application credentials and changes to identities, groups and privileged roles that could preserve access after customers addressed the original app. Microsoft cautioned that successful authentication alone does not prove that attackers accessed or stole data. ConnectWise said Oct. 22 that it was restoring services in phases over several days and told customers to keep affected connections disabled until they receive service-specific instructions. The company said its existing backup archives remained encrypted, isolated and preserved, with no indication they were compromised.

items.title: [theglobeandmail.com] B.C. voters cast ballots in close race as officials hand-count votes
items.content_html:
🎨 ✏️

British Columbia voters are choosing a 93-member legislature Saturday in a snap provincial election called two years early, with the governing New Democratic Party (NDP) and the Conservative Party of B.C. running close in final polls. During the campaign, Premier David Eby acknowledged frustration over the early election call, while both major parties promoted competing plans on affordability, health care and the economy. Eby initially cited U.S. President Donald Trump’s trade threat as a reason to seek a new mandate, then said he should have explained more clearly that the legislature had stalled under the NDP’s narrow majority. Eby also accused interim Conservative leader Lorne Doerkson of serving as a “Trojan horse” for extremists in his party; Doerkson called that characterization “absurd”. Election officials will count election-day ballots by hand because the snap vote left Elections BC too little time to prepare enough tabulators. Officials will electronically tabulate advance-voting and electoral-office ballots and report those results first. Absentee and mail-in ballots will not be included in election-night totals; they are scheduled for the final count from Nov. 6 to Nov. 10.

Tumwebaze said dependence on manual labor and unpredictable weather constrain productivity, while machinery could help farmers cultivate more land and support value-added production. Kubota and autonomy-software company Agtonomy are extending a pilot to automate orchard work such as spraying, mowing and underplant cultivation. In the United States, drone-treated acreage grew to 16.4 million acres in 2025. Equipment makers have also introduced higher-capacity grain conveyors designed to reduce harvest handling time.
